source: Phase 41 (2026-10-18): original questions on the chapters of Beast Academy Levels 1-5 and the AoPS books, written by Claude Sonnet from our own chapter summaries (docs/question-bank-beast-academy.md) and solved blind by Claude Opus (Claude Code agents, not runAi: no ai_runs rows), code-checked by lintQuestion; "checked" questions await a platform admin.

notes.BA2.01: Place value to 999 (reading hundreds/tens/ones, expanded form, value of a digit, regrouping, zero as a placeholder, 10/100 more or less, puzzles). All text-only; no figures needed. 99 questions, 33 per difficulty.
notes.BA2.02: Comparing and ordering three-digit numbers, distance between two numbers, greatest/least numbers from digits, missing digits and numbers in between, comparing amounts in hundreds/tens/ones. All text-only. 99 questions, 33 per difficulty.
notes.BA2.03: Addition within about 1,000: two-digit, three-digit, regrouping, mental strategies, several numbers, missing digits, stories. All text-only. 99 questions, 33 per difficulty.
notes.BA2.04: Subtraction within 1,000: two- and three-digit, regrouping, distance, checking with addition, missing digits. All text-only. 99 questions, 33 per difficulty.
notes.BA2.05: Expressions with + and - (left to right), parentheses, equal/unequal expressions, keeping a difference the same, balancing. All text-only; answers are whole numbers or expressions.
notes.BA2.06: Problem solving with + and -: multi-step stories, working backwards, guess and check, organized lists. Four skills only (the four the summary names), so each has about a quarter. All text-only. Some list-counting and guess-and-check items use small repeated-addition ideas (legs, coin values) rather than multiplication facts.
notes.BA2.07: All questions are text-only. Level 2 measurement: inches/feet/yards and cm/meters; conversions 12 in = 1 ft, 3 ft = 1 yd, 100 cm = 1 m. Metric and customary units are never converted into each other.
notes.BA2.08: All questions are text-only. Level 2 strategies: nearby round numbers, clever order of adding, counting numbers in a list (including lists that skip). Numbers stay below 1000 except one subtraction from 1000.
notes.BA2.09: Odd and even numbers, sums and differences, pairing up, counting odd or even numbers in a range, and odd/even patterns. All text-only. Products and divisibility rules are left out because they belong later.
notes.BA2.10: Place value to 10,000, comparing and ordering, counting by 10s, 100s and 1,000s, and adding and subtracting round numbers. All text-only; no regrouping with non-round numbers beyond a few easy cases.
notes.BA2.11: Standard algorithms with regrouping (adding and subtracting up to 4-digit numbers) and missing-digit puzzles. Missing digits are written as a box or as letters inside a horizontal equation; every puzzle was brute-force checked to have exactly one solution. All text-only. 99 questions, 33 per difficulty.
notes.BA2.12: Mixed problem solving for Level 2: number patterns, repeating patterns, organized lists and counting ways, logic puzzles (ordering, matching, number clues, one true statement), multi-step stories and working backwards / guess and check. Every logic puzzle with a search (order, matching, number clue, who-ate-it) was brute-force checked to have exactly one answer. All text-only. 99 questions, 33 per difficulty.

questions.stem: Ned has 2 sheets of 100 stickers, 2 strips of 10 stickers and 8 single stickers. How many stickers does Ned have in all?
questions.solution: 2 sheets of 100 is 200. 2 strips of 10 is 20. Add the 8 single stickers: 200 + 20 + 8 = 228.

questions.stem: Which number has 5 hundreds, 6 tens and 4 ones?
questions.solution: The hundreds digit is 5, the tens digit is 6 and the ones digit is 4, so the number is 564.

questions.stem: What digit is in the tens place of the number 571?
questions.solution: In 571 the digits are 5 hundreds, 7 tens and 1 one. The tens digit is 7.

solve.work: 571: hundreds 5, tens 7, ones 1. The tens digit is 7 (its value is 70, but the digit is 7).

questions.stem: Which of these numbers has the digit 5 in the ones place?
questions.solution: The ones place is the last digit on the right. Only 735 ends in 5.

questions.stem: Fill in the blank: $244 = 2$ hundreds + 4 tens + $\square$ ones
questions.solution: 244 has 2 hundreds, 4 tens and 4 ones. The blank is 4.

questions.stem: Pam has 896 blocks. Pam shows the number with flats (100 each), sticks (10 each) and single cubes, using as few pieces as possible. How many sticks does Pam use?
questions.solution: The fewest pieces use 8 flats, 9 sticks and 6 cubes. The tens digit tells the number of sticks: 9.

solve.work: Fewest pieces: 896 = 8 flats + 9 sticks + 6 cubes. 9 sticks.

questions.stem: Which one shows the number 973?
questions.solution: The digits of 973 are 9, 7 and 3, from the hundreds place to the ones place. So it is 9 hundreds, 7 tens, 3 ones.

questions.stem: Which is the expanded form of 269?
questions.solution: 2 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 200. 6 is in the tens place, worth 60. 9 is in the ones place. So 269 = 200 + 60 + 9.

questions.stem: What number is $700 + 60 + 1$?
questions.solution: 700 + 60 = 760, and adding 1 gives 761.

questions.stem: Find the missing number: $365 = 300 + \square + 5$
questions.solution: 365 has 6 in the tens place, and that is worth 60. The missing number is 60.

questions.stem: Uma's locker number is $800 + 10 + 1$. What is Uma's locker number?
Which number is the same as $900 + 60 + 7$?
questions.solution: The hundreds part is 900, the tens part is 60 and the ones part is 7, so the number is 967.

questions.stem: What is the value of the digit 2 in the number 126?
questions.solution: The 2 is in the tens place, so its value is 2 tens, which is 20.

solve.work: 126: the 2 is in the tens place, worth 20.

questions.stem: In the number 347, what is the value of the digit 4?
questions.solution: The 4 is in the tens place. 4 tens is 40.

solve.work: 347: the 4 is in the tens place, worth 40.

questions.stem: In 493, the digit 4 is in the hundreds place. What is the 4 worth?
questions.solution: 4 hundreds is 400.

solve.work: 4 in the hundreds place is worth 4 x 100 = 400.

questions.stem: Which digit in 241 has a value of 40?
questions.solution: A digit worth 40 is in the tens place and means 4 tens. In 241 the tens digit is 4.

solve.work: 241: 2 is worth 200, 4 is worth 40, 1 is worth 1. The digit 4.

questions.stem: In which number is the digit 9 worth 90?
questions.solution: A digit is worth 90 when it is in the tens place. Only 697 has 9 in the tens place.

questions.stem: A farmer ties carrots in bundles of 10. She has 3 bundles. How many carrots does she have?
questions.solution: 3 tens is 30.

questions.stem: Cal has 50 beads. Cal puts them into groups of 10. How many groups does Cal make?
questions.solution: 50 is 5 tens, so there are 5 groups.

questions.stem: A bakery puts 10 rolls in each bag. How many bags do 100 rolls fill?
questions.solution: 10 tens make 100, so 100 rolls fill 10 bags.

questions.stem: 2 hundreds is the same as how many tens?
questions.solution: 1 hundred is 10 tens. So 2 hundreds is 2 times 10 tens, which is 20 tens.

questions.stem: You can trade 1 hundred for 10 tens. After you trade, 3 hundreds and 8 tens becomes 2 hundreds and how many tens?
questions.solution: One hundred turns into 10 tens, so you have 8 + 10 = 18 tens.

solve.work: Trade 1 of the 3 hundreds for 10 tens: 2 hundreds and 8+10 = 18 tens. Check: 200+180 = 380.

questions.stem: What number is 5 hundreds, 0 tens and 6 ones?
questions.solution: With no tens, the digit in the tens place is 0. The number is 506.

questions.stem: Which number has 3 hundreds, 9 tens and no ones?
questions.solution: No ones means the ones digit is 0. The number is 390.

questions.stem: What digit is in the tens place of 108?
questions.solution: 108 is 1 hundred, 0 tens and 8 ones. The tens digit is 0.

questions.stem: Which number is 3 hundreds and 1 one, with no tens?
questions.solution: The tens place needs a 0 to hold it: 3, 0, 1 makes 301.

questions.solution: 10 more adds 1 to the tens digit: 442 + 10 = 452.

questions.stem: A jar has 429 marbles. Then 100 marbles are taken out. How many marbles are left?
questions.solution: Taking out 100 lowers the hundreds digit by 1: 429 - 100 = 329.

questions.skill: Ten more, ten less, hundred more, hundred less
questions.stem: Which number is 10 less than 659?
questions.solution: 10 less lowers the tens digit by 1: 659 - 10 = 649.

questions.skill: Ten more, ten less, hundred more, hundred less
questions.stem: Ivy has 647 stamps. Then Ivy buys 100 more. How many stamps does Ivy have now?
questions.solution: 100 more adds 1 to the hundreds digit: 647 + 100 = 747.

questions.stem: Which number is 100 more than 837?
questions.solution: 100 more adds 1 to the hundreds digit: 837 + 100 = 937.

questions.stem: What is the smallest 3-digit number?
questions.solution: A 3-digit number cannot start with 0. The smallest is 1 hundred, 0 tens and 0 ones: 100.

questions.stem: Which number has 6 in the hundreds place and 0 in the ones place?
questions.solution: The hundreds digit is first and the ones digit is last. Only 670 starts with 6 and ends in 0.

solve.work: Need hundreds 6, ones 0: 296 (2,_,6) no; 670 yes; 699 no; 160 (hundreds 1) no.

questions.stem: A game score is made of 6 ones, 5 hundreds and 7 tens. What is the score?
questions.solution: 5 hundreds is 500, 7 tens is 70 and 6 ones is 6. Together: 576.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a way to say 895?
questions.solution: 895 is 8 hundreds, 9 tens and 5 ones. It is also 89 tens and 5 ones, or 8 hundreds and 95 ones. But 8 hundreds, 5 tens and 9 ones swaps the tens and ones, so it is 859.

questions.stem: The digits of a number are 2, 4 and 7, from left to right. Kim writes the same digits in the opposite order. What number does Kim write?
questions.solution: The opposite order is 7, 4, 2, which is the number 742.

questions.stem: Change the tens digit of 497 to 2. What number do you get?
questions.solution: The hundreds digit 4 and the ones digit 7 stay. The new tens digit is 2, so the number is 427.

questions.stem: Which is the expanded form of 102?
questions.solution: 102 has 1 hundred, no tens and 2 ones. The expanded form is 100 + 2. There is no tens part.

questions.stem: What number is $3 + 100 + 90$?
questions.solution: The parts are in a mixed order. 100 + 90 + 3 = 193.

questions.stem: Find the missing number: $633 = \square + 30 + 3$
questions.solution: The 6 in 633 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 600.

questions.stem: Which one is NOT equal to 786?
questions.solution: 700 + 80 + 6, 700 + 86 and 780 + 6 all make 786. But 700 + 60 + 8 swaps the tens and ones and makes 768.

questions.stem: A number is written as $900 + 50 + 9$. What is the number that is 1 more?
In the number 545, what is the value of the 5 on the far left?
questions.solution: The 5 on the far left is in the hundreds place. It is worth 500. (The other 5 is in the ones place.)

solve.work: 545: leftmost 5 is in the hundreds place, worth 500.

questions.stem: In the number 294, which digit is worth the most?
questions.solution: The digit in the hundreds place is worth the most. In 294 the 2 is worth 200, more than the 9 (worth 90) or the 4 (worth 4), even though 2 is the smaller digit.

solve.work: 294: 2 worth 200, 9 worth 90, 4 worth 4. The 2 is worth the most. (Option 5 is not a digit of 294.)

questions.stem: In the number 557, how much more is the 5 on the left worth than the 5 in the middle?
questions.solution: The left 5 is worth 500 and the middle 5 is worth 50. The difference is 500 - 50 = 450.

questions.stem: In which number does the digit 5 have the greatest value?
questions.solution: The digit in the hundreds place is worth the most. Only 527 has 5 in the hundreds place, where it is worth 500.

questions.stem: Three digits in a number are worth 2, 600 and 50. What is the number?
questions.solution: 600 is the hundreds digit 6, 50 is the tens digit 5, and 2 is the ones digit. The number is 652.

questions.stem: 2 hundreds and 11 tens is what number?
Which number is the same as 3 hundreds and 15 tens?
questions.solution: 15 tens is 150, so 3 hundreds and 15 tens is 300 + 150 = 450.

questions.stem: 630 is the same as 4 hundreds and how many tens?
questions.solution: 6 hundreds and 3 tens make 630. Trading 2 hundreds for 20 tens gives 4 hundreds and 23 tens.

questions.stem: Tom has 3 bags with 100 straws in each bag and 11 bundles with 10 straws in each bundle. How many straws does Tom have in all?
questions.solution: The bags hold 300 straws. The bundles hold 11 tens, which is 110. In all: 410.

questions.stem: How many tens are in 160?
questions.solution: 160 is the same as 16 tens.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT equal to 730?
questions.solution: Trading 1 hundred for 10 tens keeps the number the same. So 6 hundreds and 13 tens is 730, and so is 5 hundreds and 23 tens. But 6 hundreds and 4 tens is only 640.

questions.stem: What number is 3 hundreds, 4 tens and 11 ones?
questions.solution: 11 ones is 1 ten and 1 one. So there are 5 tens and 1 one. The number is 351.

questions.stem: Sam's number is $800 + 9$. Cal's number is $800 + 90$. How much greater is Cal's number than Sam's?
questions.solution: Sam's number is 809. Cal's number is 890. The difference is 890 - 809 = 81.

questions.stem: Which number has a 0 in the tens place but not a 0 in the ones place?
questions.solution: 302 has 3 hundreds, 0 tens and 2 ones. The other numbers have a tens digit that is not 0, or a ones digit that is 0.

solve.work: 342 tens 4; 300 tens 0 ones 0; 340 tens 4; 302 tens 0, ones 2. Answer 302.

questions.stem: A 3-digit number has 2 in the hundreds place and 0 in the ones place. Its digits add up to 3. What is the number?
questions.solution: The ones digit is 0, so 2 + the tens digit = 3. The tens digit is 1. The number is 210.

questions.stem: A counter shows 497. You press the +10 button once. What does it show now?
questions.solution: 9 tens and 1 more ten make 10 tens, which is 1 hundred. 497 + 10 = 507.

questions.stem: What number is one ten less than 804?
questions.solution: 804 has no tens, so take 1 hundred apart into 10 tens, then take away 1 ten. 804 - 10 = 794.

questions.stem: Start at 421 and count up by tens. What is the 4th number you say after 421?
questions.solution: Counting up by tens 4 times adds 4 tens, which is 40. 421 + 40 = 461.

questions.skill: Ten more, ten less, hundred more, hundred less
questions.stem: Which number is 1 hundred and 1 ten more than 725?
questions.solution: 1 hundred and 1 ten is 110. 725 + 110 = 835.

questions.stem: I am a 3-digit number. My ones digit is 3. My tens digit is double my ones digit. My hundreds digit is 1 more than my tens digit. What number am I?
questions.solution: Double 3 is 6, so the tens digit is 6. The hundreds digit is 6 + 1 = 7. The number is 763.

questions.stem: What is the smallest 3-digit number whose digits add up to 9?
questions.solution: The hundreds digit cannot be 0, so make it 1, the smallest it can be. Then make the tens digit 0. The ones digit must be 9 - 1 = 8. The number is 108.

solve.work: Smallest hundreds digit 1; then smallest tens 0; ones 9-1-0 = 8: 108.

questions.stem: What is the greatest 3-digit number that has 0 in the ones place?
questions.solution: Use the biggest digits you can: 9 hundreds and 9 tens. The ones digit must be 0. The number is 990.

questions.stem: Which statement about 903 is true?
questions.solution: In 903 the 9 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 900. The 3 is in the ones place and is worth 3. The number has 90 tens, not 3.

solve.work: 903: 0 tens (90 tens if counting all, but '3 tens' false either way); 9 worth 900 (true); 3 worth 3. Answer: the 9 is worth 900.

questions.stem: Start with 845. Swap its tens digit and ones digit. Then add 1 to the hundreds digit. What number do you get?
questions.solution: Swapping the tens and ones digits gives 854. Adding 1 to the hundreds digit gives 954.

questions.stem: Which number has 2 more hundreds, 3 fewer tens and the same ones as 441?
questions.solution: 441 is 4 hundreds, 4 tens and 1 one. Now use 6 hundreds, 1 ten and 1 one: 611.

questions.stem: What number is $200 + 130 + 1$?
questions.solution: 130 is 1 hundred and 3 tens. So the sum is 3 hundreds, 3 tens and 1 one: 331.

questions.stem: Which sum does NOT equal 465?
questions.solution: 300 + 160 + 5 and 400 + 50 + 15 both make 465. But 300 + 70 + 5 makes only 375.

questions.stem: Write 367 as a sum of its hundreds part, tens part and ones part. What is the greatest part minus the least part?
questions.solution: 367 = 300 + 60 + 7. The greatest part is 300 and the least is 7. 300 - 7 = 293.

questions.stem: A number has digits worth 800, 40 and 1. How much greater is the value of the hundreds digit than the values of the other two digits put together?
questions.solution: The other two digits are worth 40 + 1 = 41. 800 - 41 = 759.

questions.stem: Which pair of numbers has a 4 that is worth the same amount in both numbers?
questions.solution: A 4 is worth 40 in the tens place, 400 in the hundreds place and 4 in the ones place. Only in "148 and 843" is the 4 in the same place in both numbers (the tens place, worth 40).

solve.work: 294 (4 ones) vs 946 (4 tens): no. 148 (4 tens) vs 843 (4 tens): both 40, yes. 774 (ones) vs 475 (hundreds): no. 142 (tens) vs 451 (hundreds): no.

questions.stem: How many numbers from 200 to 299 have the digit 3 in the tens place?
questions.solution: The numbers are 230, 231, 232 and so on up to 239. That is 10 numbers, one for each ones digit.

questions.stem: Add the value of the hundreds digit of 468 to the value of its ones digit. Then take away the value of its tens digit. What do you get?
questions.solution: The hundreds digit is worth 400, the ones digit is worth 8 and the tens digit is worth 60. 400 + 8 - 60 = 348.

questions.stem: What number is 6 hundreds, 11 tens and 12 ones?
questions.solution: 6 hundreds is 600, 11 tens is 110 and there are 12 ones. 600 + 110 + 12 = 722.

questions.stem: Put 22 tens together with 6 hundreds. What number do you get?
Tom has 655 straws and ties as many bundles of 10 straws as Tom can. How many bundles does Tom make?
questions.solution: The 5 ones cannot make a bundle. The rest is 650, which is 65 tens. So Tom makes 65 bundles.

solve.work: 655 = 65 tens + 5 ones, so 65 bundles (5 straws left).

questions.stem: How many ways can you make 700 using only flats worth 100 and sticks worth 10? (Using no flats is one way, and using no sticks is one way.)
questions.solution: You can use 0, 1, 2, up to 7 flats, and fill the rest with sticks. That is 7 + 1 = 8 ways.

solve.work: Flats can be 0..7; sticks fill the rest (700 - 100f is a multiple of 10). 8 ways.

questions.stem: Which number is the same as 2 hundreds, 12 tens and 12 ones?
Fill in the blank: $922 = \square$ tens + 2 ones
questions.solution: Take away the 2 ones: 920 is 92 tens. The blank is 92.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a way to make 631 from hundreds, tens and ones?
questions.solution: Trading 1 hundred for 10 tens, or 1 ten for 10 ones, keeps the number the same. The first three do that. But 5 hundreds, 13 tens and 11 ones trades twice and has 10 too many ones: it is 641.

questions.stem: How many numbers from 800 to 899 have a 0 in the tens place?
questions.solution: The numbers are 800, 801, 802 and so on up to 809. That is 10 numbers.

questions.stem: How many different 3-digit numbers can you make with the digits 7, 0 and 2, using each digit once? (A 3-digit number cannot start with 0.)
questions.solution: The first digit is 7 or 2. Starting with 7: 702 and 720. Starting with 2: 207 and 270. That is 4 numbers.

questions.stem: A counter shows 709. What does it show one number later?
questions.solution: After 709 comes 710: the 9 ones and 1 more make a new ten, so there is 1 ten and 0 ones.

questions.solution: 200 is 1 hundred and 10 tens. Take away 1 ten: 1 hundred and 9 tens, which is 190.

questions.solution: 3 presses add 30. 195 + 30 = 225.

questions.stem: Pat counts up by 100s, starting with 667. Pat stops before the numbers go past 999. How many numbers does Pat say, counting 667?
questions.solution: The numbers are 667, 767, and so on, one more hundred each time, until the hundreds digit reaches 9. The hundreds digit goes 6, 7, ..., 9, which is 4 numbers.

questions.stem: A 3-digit number has 1 in the ones place. Its tens digit is 2 more than its ones digit. Its hundreds digit is 2 more than its tens digit. What is the number?
questions.solution: Ones digit 1. Tens digit 1 + 2 = 3. Hundreds digit 3 + 2 = 5. The number is 531.

questions.stem: I am a 3-digit number. All three of my digits are the same. My digits add up to 6. What number am I?
questions.solution: Three equal digits add to 6, so each digit is 6 divided by 3, which is 2. The number is 222.

questions.stem: How many 3-digit numbers have all three digits the same?
questions.solution: The hundreds digit can be 1, 2, 3, up to 9 (not 0). Once it is chosen, the other digits must match it. That gives 9 numbers: 111, 222, up to 999.

questions.stem: Which number is made of exactly 38 tens and 5 ones?
questions.solution: 38 tens is 380. Add 5 ones: 380 + 5 = 385.

questions.stem: Tom builds 954 from flats worth 100, sticks worth 10 and cubes worth 1. What is the fewest number of pieces Tom can use?
questions.solution: Use as few pieces as possible by never keeping 10 of a kind. That is 9 flats, 5 sticks and 4 cubes: 9 + 5 + 4 = 18 pieces.

questions.stem: What is the greatest 3-digit number whose digits add up to 11?
questions.solution: Make the hundreds digit as big as possible: 9. Then 9 + the tens digit + the ones digit = 11. Make the tens digit as big as it can be, 2, so the ones digit is 0. The number is 920.

solve.work: Hundreds 9, then tens as big as possible: 11-9 = 2, ones 0: 920.

questions.stem: How many numbers from 700 to 799 have the same tens digit and ones digit?
questions.solution: They are 700, 711, 722, up to 799. That is 10 numbers.

questions.stem: A 3-digit number has 4 in the hundreds place. Its tens digit is double its ones digit. Its digits add up to 7. What is the number?
questions.solution: The tens digit and ones digit add up to 7 - 4 = 3. The tens digit is double the ones digit, so the ones digit is 3 divided by 3, which is 1, and the tens digit is 2. The number is 421.

questions.stem: How many different 3-digit numbers can you make with the digits 2, 1 and 6, using each digit once?
questions.solution: Pick any of the 3 digits to go first, then either of the 2 left to go next, and the last digit goes at the end. That is 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 numbers.

questions.stem: Look at the numbers 613 and 378. Which comparison is true?
questions.solution: Compare the hundreds first. 613 has 6 hundreds and 378 has only 3 hundreds, so 613 > 378.

questions.stem: Which is greater, 377 or 803? Type the greater number.
questions.solution: 803 has 8 hundreds and 377 has 3 hundreds. More hundreds means a greater number, so 803 is greater.

questions.stem: Which number is less than 620?
questions.solution: 620 has 6 hundreds. Only the number with fewer than 6 hundreds is less than 620.

solve.work: 740, 650, 722 are all above 620; 568 has 5 hundreds, so 568 < 620.

questions.stem: Ana has 801 stickers, Leo has 673, Ned has 272 and Uma has 526. Who has the most stickers?
questions.solution: The most hundreds wins here. Ana has 801 stickers, the greatest number.

questions.stem: Which sentence is NOT true?
questions.solution: 288 < 343 < 636 < 769, so 343 is less than 769. The sentence 343 > 769 is not true.

solve.work: 343 > 769 is false (3 hundreds < 7 hundreds). 636 > 288, 288 < 343, 769 > 636 are true.

questions.stem: One jar has 243 buttons and another jar has 177 buttons. How many buttons are in the jar that has fewer?
questions.solution: 177 has fewer hundreds than 243, so 177 is the smaller number.

solve.work: 177 < 243, so the jar with fewer has 177.

questions.stem: Which number is greater than 368?
questions.solution: 368 has 3 hundreds. Only the number with more hundreds is greater than 368.

solve.work: 367, 359, 299 are less than 368; 423 has 4 hundreds, greater.

questions.stem: Which list is in order from least to greatest?
questions.solution: Least to greatest means the smallest number goes first. 107 < 506 < 762.

questions.stem: Put 554, 846 and 390 in order from least to greatest. What is the middle number?
questions.solution: In order: 390, 554, 846. The middle number is 554.

questions.stem: What is the greatest of these numbers: 756, 484, 684, 801?
questions.solution: Compare the hundreds digits. 801 has the most hundreds, so it is the greatest.

questions.stem: Which of these numbers is the least?
questions.solution: The least number has the fewest hundreds. That is 141.

solve.work: 141 has 1 hundred, the fewest. Least is 141.

questions.stem: Mia wrote three numbers with the biggest first. Which list did Mia write?
questions.solution: Greatest to least means the biggest number goes first: 496, then 218, then 184.

questions.stem: Four towers are built from blocks. They have 526, 346, 408 and 264 blocks. How many blocks are in the tallest tower?
questions.solution: The tallest tower has the most blocks. The greatest number is 526.

questions.stem: How far apart are 400 and 800?
questions.solution: 8 hundreds - 4 hundreds = 4 hundreds, which is 400.

questions.stem: How much greater is 773 than 743?
questions.solution: Both numbers have 7 hundreds and 3 ones. The tens are 7 and 4, which are 3 tens apart: 30.

questions.stem: Zoe walked 813 steps and Ben walked 815 steps. How many more steps did Ben walk?
questions.solution: Only the ones are different: 5 - 3 = 2.

questions.stem: How far is it from 210 up to 250?
Start at 330 and count up by tens until you reach 380. How many tens do you count?
questions.solution: Each count adds 1 ten. From 3 tens to 8 tens is 5 counts.

questions.solution: Put the biggest digit in the hundreds place, the next biggest in the tens place and the smallest in the ones place: 631.

questions.skill: Greatest or least number from digits
questions.stem: Use each of the digits 9, 6 and 8 once to make the least number you can. What number do you make?
questions.solution: Put the smallest digit in the hundreds place, the next smallest in the tens place and the biggest in the ones place: 689.

questions.skill: Greatest or least number from digits
questions.stem: Which is the greatest number you can make with the digits 5, 4 and 3, using each digit once?
questions.solution: The greatest number has the biggest digit first: 543.

questions.solution: The least number has the smallest digit first: 168.

questions.stem: Ned has three cards with the numbers 4, 3 and 2. Ned puts them in a row to make the biggest number possible. What number is it?
questions.solution: Biggest digit first: 4, 3, 2. The number is 432.

questions.skill: Greatest or least number from digits
questions.stem: Ned has three digit cards: 3, 0 and 7. Ned lines them up to make the largest number possible. What is the number?
questions.solution: Put the biggest digit 7 first, then 3, then 0: 730.

questions.solution: 23 + 77 = 100, so add those two first. Then 100 + 36 = 136.

questions.stem: $2? + 49 = 78$ The ? stands for one digit. What digit is it?
questions.solution: Ones: ? + 9 makes 18, so it ends in 8: ? = 9. Check: 29 + 49 = 78.

questions.stem: Which digit goes in place of the ? $?4 + 26 = 70$
questions.solution: The ones make 4 + 6 = 10, so 1 ten is regrouped. Tens: ? + 2 + 1 = 7, so ? = 4.

questions.stem: $3?6 + 415 = 771$ What digit is the ?
questions.solution: The ones make 6 + 5 = 11, so 1 ten is regrouped. Tens: ? + 1 + 1 = 7, so ? = 5.

questions.stem: What digit goes in the ? to make this true? $279 + 422 = 7?1$
questions.solution: 279 + 422 = 701. The tens digit of 701 is 0.

questions.stem: $?77 + 147 = 424$ What digit is the ?
questions.solution: The ones and tens both regroup. Hundreds: ? + 1 + 1 = 4, so ? = 2. Check: 277 + 147 = 424.

questions.stem: Which digit goes in the box? $597 + 2\square = 626$
questions.solution: The ones must end in 6: 7 + 9 = 16. So the box is 9. Check: 597 + 29 = 626.

questions.stem: Val has 48 balloons and wants 71. This sentence shows the problem: $48 + ? = 71$. How many more balloons does Val need?
I think of a number and add 50. The answer is 108. What number did I think of?
questions.solution: The number plus 50 is 108, so the number is 108 - 50 = 58. Check: 58 + 50 = 108.

questions.stem: Which story is solved by $52 + 49$?
choices: Cal has 52 crayons and Zoe has 49. How many more does Cal have?
Cal has 52 crayons and Zoe has 49. How many in all?
Cal has 52 crayons and loses 49 of them. How many are left?
Cal has 52 crayons. Zoe has 49 fewer. How many does Zoe have?
questions.answer: Cal has 52 crayons and Zoe has 49. How many in all?
questions.solution: Putting 52 and 49 together means adding: 52 + 49. The others ask how many more, how many are left, or how many fewer, which are subtraction.

solve.answer: Cal has 52 crayons and Zoe has 49. How many in all?
solve.work: 52 + 49 joins both amounts: how many in all.

questions.stem: Eli has 73 beads. Pam has 51 more beads than Eli. How many beads does Pam have?
questions.solution: Pam has 51 more than 73, so 73 + 51 = 124.

questions.stem: A library has 131 picture books on one shelf. It gets 58 more books on Monday and 42 more books on Tuesday. How many picture books does it have then?
What is the sum of the greatest two-digit number and the smallest two-digit number?
questions.solution: The greatest two-digit number is 99 and the smallest is 10. 99 + 10 = 109.

questions.stem: How much greater is the larger of $39 + 63$ and $47 + 83$ than the smaller one?
Two of the numbers 54, 26, 43, 14 add up to 80. Which two?
questions.solution: 54 + 26 = 80. The other pairs make 68, 40, 57.

questions.stem: Eli adds two different numbers from this list: 10, 20, 30, 40. He tries every pair. How many different sums can he make?
questions.solution: The pairs make 10+20=30, 10+30=40, 10+40=50, 20+30=50, 20+40=60 and 30+40=70. The sums are 30, 40, 50, 60 and 70 (50 comes up twice), so there are 5 different sums.

questions.stem: The tens digit of a number is 3 and its ones digit is 2. Write the digits the other way round to make a second number. What is the sum of the two numbers?
questions.solution: The numbers are 32 and 23. 32 + 23 = 55.

questions.stem: Use each of the digits 1, 2, 5, 7, 8, 9 exactly once to make two three-digit numbers. What is the smallest sum the two numbers can have?
questions.solution: To make the sum small, put the two smallest digits (1 and 2) in the hundreds places, the next two (5 and 7) in the tens places, and the largest two (8 and 9) in the ones places. The sum is 300 + 120 + 17 = 437.

solve.work: Smallest hundreds 1 and 2, tens 5 and 7, ones 8 and 9: 300 + 120 + 17 = 437 (e.g. 158 + 279).

questions.stem: A game has 469 points on level one and 375 points on level two. A bonus adds 30 more points. What is the total number of points?
questions.solution: Ones: 9 + 5 = 14. Write 4 and regroup 1 into the next place. Tens: 6 + 7 + 1 = 14. Write 4 and regroup 1 into the next place. Hundreds: 4 + 3 + 1 = 8. The sum is 844. Then 844 + 30 = 874.

questions.stem: Raj walked 269 steps on Saturday and 342 steps on Sunday. Uma walked 326 steps on Saturday and 294 steps on Sunday. Who walked more steps in all?
choices: It is not possible to tell
questions.solution: Raj: 269 + 342 = 611. Uma: 326 + 294 = 620. Uma walked more.

questions.stem: Write the digits of 213 in the opposite order to make a new number. What is 213 plus the new number?
questions.solution: The new number is 312. 213 + 312 = 525.

questions.stem: Which pair of numbers adds up to 500?
questions.solution: 203 + 297 = 500. The other pairs make 510, 490, 520.

questions.stem: Which sum is equal to $598 + 331$?
questions.solution: 598 is 2 less than 600. Moving 2 from the second number to the first keeps the sum: 598 + 331 = 600 + 329.

questions.stem: 398 is 2 less than 400 and 397 is 3 less than 400. Use this to work out $398 + 397$.
questions.solution: 400 + 400 = 800. But we added 5 too many (2 and 3), so 800 - 5 = 795.

questions.stem: Break 232 into 200 + 30 + 2. Add the three parts to 237 one at a time. What number do you end with?
You know that $400 + 400 = 800$. Use it to find $399 + 400$.
Which sum is the greatest? Think about how far each number is from 400.
questions.solution: Each number is near 400, so compare the small differences. 402 + 403 = 805; 403 + 398 = 801; 399 + 397 = 796; 398 + 401 = 799. The greatest is 805.

questions.stem: 295 is close to 300 and 296 is close to 300. What is $295 + 296$?
questions.solution: 300 + 300 = 600. 295 is 5 less than 300 and 296 is 4 less than 300, so take away 5 + 4 = 9: 600 - 9 = 591.

questions.stem: What is $92 + 25 + 175 + 108$? Find numbers that add to a round number.
What is $19 + 20 + 21 + 22 + 23$? The middle number may help.
questions.solution: The numbers are spread evenly around 21. 19 + 23 = 42, which is 2 groups of 21, and 20 + 22 is another 2 groups. With the middle 21, there are 5 groups of 21. Adding: 42 + 42 + 21 = 105.
8 + 18 + 28 + 38: each number is 2 less than 10, 20, 30, 40. That total is 100, and we took away 8 in all: 100 - 8 = 92.

questions.stem: What is the sum of all the whole numbers from 31 to 40? (31, 32, 33, and so on up to 40.)
questions.solution: Pair the first with the last: 31 + 40 = 71. The next pair also makes 71, and so on. There are 5 pairs, so 355.

questions.stem: A school has 145 students in Grade 1, 167 in Grade 2, 133 in Grade 3 and 155 in Grade 4. How many students are there in these four grades?
questions.solution: Find two numbers that make 300: 155 + 145 = 300 and 133 + 167 = 300. So the total is 300 + 300 = 600.

questions.stem: Each of these numbers is close to 100: 101, 100, 102, 99, 98. What is their total?
questions.solution: Each is 100 plus or minus a little: the small amounts (-2, +1, -1, +2, 0) cancel out and add to 0. So the total is 5 x 100 = 500.

questions.stem: A and B are digits. $3A + B9 = 96$ What is A + B?
questions.solution: Ones: A + 9 ends in 6, so A = 7. That makes 1 ten. Tens: 3 + B + 1 = 9, so B = 5. A + B = 7 + 5 = 12.

solve.work: Ones: A + 9 ends in 6, so A = 7, carry 1. Tens: 3 + B + 1 = 9, B = 5. 37 + 59 = 96. A + B = 12.

questions.stem: A and B are digits. $4A7 + 5B8 = 985$ What is A + B?
questions.solution: Ones: 7 + 8 = 15, so 1 ten is regrouped. Tens: A + B + 1 = 8, so A + B = 7. The hundreds work out without any further regrouping.

solve.work: Ones 7 + 8 = 15, carry 1. Hundreds 4 + 5 = 9, so no carry from tens: A + B + 1 = 8, A + B = 7.

questions.stem: One number ends in the digit 4. Another number ends in the digit 9. What is the ones digit of their sum?
questions.solution: 4 + 9 = 13. The ones digit of 13 is 3, because the 1 ten is regrouped into the tens place.

questions.stem: A and B are digits. $7A4 + 2B = 731$ The first number has three digits and the second has two. What is A + B?
questions.solution: Ones: 4 + B ends in 1, so B = 7. Then A is in the tens place of the first number. Tens: A + 2 + 1 ends in 3, so A = 0. A + B = 0 + 7 = 7.

solve.work: Ones: 4 + B ends in 1, B = 7, carry 1. Tens: A + 2 + 1 = 3, A = 0. 704 + 27 = 731. A + B = 7.

questions.stem: $5? + 47 > 100$ The ? is one digit. What is the smallest digit that can replace the ?
questions.solution: 5? + 47 is 97 + ?. For this to be more than 100, ? must be at least 4: 97 + 4 = 101. With 3 it makes 100, which is not more than 100.

questions.stem: The same digit goes in both boxes. $\square2 + \square9 = 91$ What digit is it?
questions.solution: The ones make 2 + 9 = 11, so 1 ten is regrouped. Tens: box + box + 1 = 9, so the two boxes make 8, and each box is 4. Check: 42 + 49 = 91.

questions.stem: I think of a number. I add 45, then I add 15. The answer is 104. What number did I think of?
questions.solution: 45 + 15 = 60. So the number plus 60 is 104, and the number is 104 - 60 = 44.

questions.stem: How many ways can you write 10 as the sum of two whole numbers, each at least 1? Order does not matter, so 3 + 7 and 7 + 3 count as the same way.
questions.solution: List them from the smallest first number: 1 + 9, 2 + 8, 3 + 7, 4 + 6, 5 + 5. That is 5 ways.

questions.stem: Zoe has 55 blocks. Ned has 14 more than Zoe. Val has 17 more than Ned. How many blocks do the three children have in all?
Two numbers add up to 106. One is 30 more than the other. What is the greater number?
questions.solution: If the numbers were equal, they would add to 106 - 30 = 76, so the smaller is 38. The greater is 38 + 30 = 68. Check: 38 + 68 = 106.

questions.stem: A book has 132 pages. Ben read 40 pages on Monday and 62 pages on Tuesday. The sentence $40 + 62 + ? = 132$ shows the problem. How many pages are left to read?
What is $87 - 20$?
questions.solution: Take 20 away from 87: 80 - 20 = 60, and the 7 ones stay. So 87 - 20 = 67.

questions.stem: Gus has 55 stamps. Gus gives 30 of them to Jo. How many stamps does Gus have left?
questions.solution: 55 - 30 = 25. Giving away 3 tens changes only the tens digit.

questions.stem: Find 88 minus 36.
questions.solution: Ones: 8 - 6 = 2. Tens: 8 - 3 = 5. The difference is 52.

questions.stem: Which number is $72 - 22$?
questions.solution: Ones: 2 - 2 = 0. Tens: 7 - 2 = 5. The difference is 50.

questions.stem: Start at 78. Take away 10, then take away 10 again, then take away 10 again. What number is left?
questions.solution: Taking away 10 three times takes away 30. 78 - 30 = 48.
7 - 2 = 5, so the difference is 5 hundreds, which is 500.

questions.stem: A store has 810 toy cars. It sells 400 of them. How many toy cars are left?
questions.solution: Only the hundreds change: 810 - 400 = 410.

questions.stem: What is $584 - 3$?
questions.solution: The ones: 4 - 3 = 1. The other digits stay the same. So 584 - 3 = 581.

questions.stem: Which number is $762 - 532$?
questions.solution: Ones: 2 - 2 = 0. Tens: 6 - 3 = 3. Hundreds: 7 - 5 = 2. The difference is 230.

questions.stem: A road is 366 meters long. 20 meters of it are paved. How many meters of the road are not paved?
questions.solution: 366 - 20 = 346. Only the tens digit changes, from 6 to 4.

questions.stem: 61 is 5 tens and 11 ones. Use this to work out $61 - 4$.
questions.solution: With 11 ones you can take away 4 ones: 11 - 4 = 7. The 5 tens stay. So the answer is 5 tens and 7 ones, which is 57.

solve.work: 5 tens and 11 ones minus 4 ones = 5 tens 7 ones = 57.

questions.stem: What is $100 - 90$?
questions.solution: 100 is 10 tens. Take away 9 tens: 1 ten is left, which is 10.

questions.stem: Which number is 10 less than 234?
questions.solution: 10 less than 234 is 224: the tens digit goes down by 1.

questions.stem: What number is 100 less than 264?
questions.solution: 100 less takes 1 off the hundreds digit. 264 - 100 = 164.

questions.stem: Which is equal to $82 - 6$?
questions.solution: Take away 2 first to reach 80, then take away the other 4, because 2 + 4 = 6. So 82 - 6 = 80 - 4.

questions.stem: To subtract 9, you can take away 10 and then add 1. What is $49 - 9$?
Fay is on page 30 of a book and wants to get to page 70. How many pages does Fay still have to go?
questions.solution: The distance from 30 to 70 is 70 - 30 = 40.

questions.stem: What is the difference between 73 and 31?
questions.solution: The difference is the bigger number minus the smaller one: 73 - 31 = 42.

questions.stem: Kim is 11 years old. Cal is 13 years old. How many years older is Cal than Kim?
questions.solution: 13 - 11 = 2. Cal is 2 years older.

questions.stem: A short tree is 14 inches tall. A tall tree is 56 inches tall. How many inches taller is the tall tree?
questions.solution: Ones: 6 - 4 = 2. Tens: 5 - 1 = 4. The difference is 42.

questions.stem: Which pair of numbers is exactly 30 apart?
questions.solution: 52 - 22 = 30, so 22 and 52 are 30 apart. The other pairs are 40, 20 and 39 apart.

questions.stem: A trail is 100 meters long. Mia has walked 30 meters. How many more meters is it to the end of the trail?
questions.solution: The distance left is 100 - 30 = 70.

questions.stem: Leo knows that $3 + 9 = 12$. What is $12 - 3$?
questions.solution: Adding and taking away undo each other. Since 3 + 9 = 12, taking 3 away from 12 leaves 9.

questions.stem: Which addition checks that 51 - 21 = 30 is right?
questions.solution: To check a subtraction, add the answer to the number taken away: 30 + 21 = 51. You get back to the number you started with.

solve.work: Difference plus the number taken away gives the start: 30 + 21 = 51.

questions.stem: Zoe says that 67 - 11 = 56. To check, Zoe adds 56 + 11. What number does Zoe get?
questions.solution: 56 + 11 = 67. It matches the number Zoe started with, so the answer is right.

questions.stem: Which answer is right for $53 - 11$? Check each one by adding 11.
questions.solution: 42 + 11 = 53, so 42 is right. Each other answer plus 11 does not make 53.

questions.stem: Which subtraction sentence goes with $28 + 45 = 73$?
questions.solution: 28 + 45 = 73 is in a family with 73 - 28 = 45 and 73 - 45 = 28. The other sentences are not true.

questions.stem: Mia says that 64 - 41 = 23. Val says that 64 - 41 = 13. Check by adding. Who is right?
questions.solution: The right answer is 23, because 23 + 41 = 64. The other answer, 13, plus 41 makes 54, not 64.
