questions.stem: Hal and Raj have 18 stickers together. Hal has 10 more stickers than Raj. How many stickers does Hal have?
questions.solution: If Hal gave away the 10 extra stickers, both would have the same: 18 - 10 = 8, so each would have 4. Then Hal has 4 + 10 = 14.

questions.stem: I am a 2-digit number. My two digits are the same. I am between 80 and 100. I am even. What number am I?
questions.solution: Numbers with two matching digits are 11, 22, 33, ..., 99. The ones between 80 and 100 are 88, 99. Only 88 is even.

questions.stem: Leo is 10 years old. Raj is 2 years older than Leo. Eli is 4 years younger than Raj. Which sentence is true?
choices: Eli is the same age as Leo.
questions.solution: Raj is 10 + 2 = 12. Eli is 12 - 4 = 8. So the ages are Leo 10, Raj 12, Eli 8. Only "Raj is older than Leo." matches.

solve.work: Leo 10, Raj 12, Eli 8. Only 'Raj is older than Leo' is true.

questions.stem: A ball, a block and a bear are put in three boxes, one thing in each: the small box, the medium box, the large box. The ball is in the large box. The bear is not in the large box. The bear is in the small box. Which box holds the block?
questions.solution: The only way to place all three things so that every clue is true is: the ball in the large box; the block in the medium box; the bear in the small box. So the block is in the medium box.

solve.work: Ball large, bear small, block medium.

questions.stem: A farmer has 3 baskets with 11 eggs in each. 6 eggs break. The farmer sells 15 of the eggs that are not broken. How many eggs are left?
questions.solution: 3 x 11 = 33 eggs. After the broken ones: 33 - 6 = 27. After selling: 27 - 15 = 12.

questions.stem: Pam is 8 years old. Cal is 2 years older than Pam. Dee is 3 times as old as Cal. How old will Dee be in 3 years?
questions.solution: Cal is 8 + 2 = 10. Dee is 3 x 10 = 30. In 3 years: 30 + 3 = 33.

questions.stem: A train has 6 cars with 9 seats in each car. At first, 16 seats are empty. Then 10 more people get on the train and take seats. How many seats are taken now?
questions.solution: All the seats: 6 x 9 = 54. Taken at first: 54 - 16 = 38. After 10 more people: 38 + 10 = 48.

questions.stem: Uma has 49 stickers. Uma gives 14 stickers to Dee and 17 stickers to Mia. Then Uma is given 21 new stickers. How many stickers does Uma have now?
questions.solution: 14 + 17 = 31 stickers given away. 49 - 31 = 18. Then 18 + 21 = 39.

questions.stem: Eli saves 6 dollars every week for 6 weeks. Then Eli spends 11 dollars on a toy. How many dollars does Eli have left?
questions.solution: Saved: 6 x 6 = 36 dollars. Spent 11: 36 - 11 = 25 dollars.

questions.skill: Working backwards and guess and check
questions.stem: I think of a number and add 7. Then I double my answer. The result is 26. What number did I think of?
questions.solution: Work backwards. Undo "double": half of 26 is 13. Undo "add 7": 13 - 7 = 6. Check: 6 + 7 = 13, doubled is 26.

questions.skill: Working backwards and guess and check
questions.stem: I think of a number and subtract 3. Then I multiply my answer by 2. The result is 26. What number did I think of?
questions.solution: Work backwards. Undo "multiply by 2": 26 / 2 = 13. Undo "subtract 3": 13 + 3 = 16. Check: 16 - 3 = 13, times 2 is 26.

questions.skill: Working backwards and guess and check
questions.stem: Tom has only 2-cent stamps and 5-cent stamps. He has 5 stamps, worth 19 cents in all. How many 5-cent stamps does he have?
questions.solution: Guess and check. Try 3 stamps worth 5 cents and 2 stamps worth 2 cents: 3 x 5 = 15 and 2 x 2 = 4. 15 + 4 = 19. That works. Other guesses give a different total.

questions.skill: Working backwards and guess and check
questions.stem: I think of a number and cut it in half. Then I add 3. The result is 9. What number did I think of?
questions.solution: Work backwards. Undo "add 3": 9 - 3 = 6. Undo "cut in half" by doubling: 6 x 2 = 12. Check: half of 12 is 6, plus 3 is 9.

questions.skill: Working backwards and guess and check
questions.stem: Which number goes in the box to make this true? $\square - 6 + 5 = 27$
questions.solution: Work backwards. Undo "+ 5": 27 - 5 = 22. Undo "- 6": 22 + 6 = 28. Check: 28 - 6 + 5 = 27.

questions.stem: A pattern begins 2, 8, 14, 20, and goes up by the same amount each time. What is the 21st number in the pattern?
questions.solution: The 21st number is 20 jumps after the first number: 2 + 20 x 6 = 122.

questions.stem: A pattern begins 6, 13, 20, 27, and goes up by the same amount each time. What is the first number in the pattern that is greater than 102?
questions.solution: Every number is 6 plus a multiple of 7. Counting up from 6 by 7, the last number not greater than 102 is 97, and the next number is 104.

questions.stem: A pattern starts at 1 and goes up by 4 each time. Which of these numbers is NOT in the pattern?
questions.solution: Every number in the pattern is 1 plus a multiple of 4. 45, 37, 41 are all of that form, but 42 - 1 = 41, and 41 is not a multiple of 4.

solve.work: Terms are 1 more than a multiple of 4: 37, 41, 45 are; 42 is not.

questions.stem: Squares are made from matchsticks and joined in a row. One square uses 4 matchsticks. Two squares joined in a row use 7 matchsticks. Three squares joined in a row use 10 matchsticks. How many matchsticks do 10 squares joined in a row use?
questions.solution: Each new square adds 3 matchsticks. So 10 squares use 4 + 3 x 9 = 31 matchsticks.

questions.stem: Here is a pattern: 2, 4, 7, 11, 16, ... The gaps between the numbers are 2, 3, 4, 5 and keep growing by 1 each time. What is the 9th number in the pattern?
questions.solution: The gaps keep growing by 1: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. The numbers are 2, 4, 7, 11, 16, 22, 29, 37, 46. The 9th is 46.

questions.stem: A fence has boards painted in this pattern: 2 red boards, then 4 blue boards, over and over. How many blue boards are in the first 34 boards?
questions.solution: One group is 6 boards. 34 = 5 groups and 4 boards over. The groups have 20 blue boards. The 4 extra boards are 2 red and 2 blue. Total 20 + 2 = 22.

solve.work: 30 boards = 5 units, 20 blue; boards 31-32 red, 33-34 blue. 22.

questions.stem: The six letters ABCCDD are written over and over: A B C C D D A B C C D D ... What is the 54th letter?
questions.solution: The pattern repeats every 6 letters. 54 = 48 + 6, so the 54th letter matches letter number 6 of ABCCDD, which is D.

solve.work: 54 = 9 x 6, so the 54th is the last of a unit: D.

questions.stem: Cards are laid out in the order 4, 2, 1, 4, 2, 1, 4, 2, 1, and so on, over and over. What is the total of the first 17 cards?
questions.solution: One group adds to 4 + 2 + 1 = 7. 17 cards is 5 groups and 2 extra cards. 5 x 7 = 35, plus 4 + 2 makes 41.

solve.work: 15 cards = 5 units of total 7 = 35; cards 16, 17 are 4, 2. 41.

questions.stem: Beads are strung in this pattern of 5 beads, over and over: red, red, blue, red, blue. The pattern keeps repeating. At which bead number is the 7th blue bead?
questions.solution: Each group of 5 beads has 2 blue beads. 7 blue beads need 3 full groups (15 beads) and then blue bead number 1 of a group. Counting it out, the 7th blue bead is bead 18.

solve.work: Blues at 3 and 5 of each unit of 5. Units 1-3 give 6 blues (last at 15); 7th blue at 15+3 = 18.

questions.stem: Four different toy cars are put in a row on a table. How many different orders can they be put in?
questions.solution: There are 4 choices for the first place, then 3 for the second, 2 for the third and 1 for the last. 4 x 3 x 2 x 1 = 24.

questions.stem: You have four digit cards: 1, 3, 5, 9. You make 2-digit numbers by choosing a tens digit and a ones digit (each card may be used only once in a number, so both digits are different). How many different 2-digit numbers can you make?
questions.solution: 4 choices for the tens digit, then 3 choices left for the ones digit: 4 x 3 = 12.

questions.stem: There are 5 teams in a league. Every team plays every other team once. How many games are played in all?
questions.solution: Count without repeats: the first one has 4 partners, the next has 3 more, and so on. 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10.

questions.stem: Two number cubes each show 1 to 6. One is red and one is blue, so a red 2 and a blue 6 is different from a red 6 and a blue 2. In how many different ways can the two cubes add up to 8?
questions.solution: List the (red, blue) pairs that add to 8: (2, 6), (3, 5), (4, 4), (5, 3), (6, 2). That is 5 ways.

questions.stem: A child climbs 4 stairs. Each time, the child steps up either 1 stair or 2 stairs. In how many different ways can the child climb all 4 stairs?
questions.solution: Let ways(k) be the number of ways to climb k stairs. ways(1) = 1, ways(2) = 2, and each later number is the sum of the two before it (the last step was 1 stair or 2 stairs): 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13. So 4 stairs can be climbed in 5 ways.

questions.stem: How many different pairs of two different whole numbers from 1 to 9 add up to 11? (Order does not matter, so 2 + 5 and 5 + 2 count as one pair.)
questions.solution: List them from the smallest first number: 2 + 9; 3 + 8; 4 + 7; 5 + 6. That is 4 pairs.

questions.stem: One of three children ate the last cookie. Each child says one sentence, and exactly one of the three sentences is true. Gus says: "Jo did not eat it." Ben says: "I did not eat it." Jo says: "I ate it." Who ate the cookie?
questions.solution: Try each child as the one who ate the cookie and count the true sentences. Only when Ben ate it are exactly one of the three sentences true, so Ben ate the cookie.

solve.work: If Jo: Ben and Jo true (2). If Gus: Gus and Ben true (2). If Ben: only Gus true (1). Ben.

questions.stem: Five children stand in a line. Ben is somewhere ahead of Raj. Raj is right behind Dee. Zoe is right behind Raj. Kim is right behind Zoe. Who is third in the line?
questions.solution: The only order that fits every clue is Ben, Dee, Raj, Zoe, Kim (from the front). So Raj is third.

solve.work: Dee, Raj, Zoe, Kim back to back; Ben ahead of Raj and not between Dee and Raj, so Ben first. Ben, Dee, Raj, Zoe, Kim. Third Raj.

questions.stem: I am a 2-digit number. My two digits add up to 14. My tens digit is 4 more than my ones digit. What number am I?
questions.solution: Two digits that add to 14 and differ by 4: the bigger digit is (14 + 4) / 2 = 9 and the smaller is (14 - 4) / 2 = 5. The tens digit is the bigger one, so I am 95.

solve.work: Tens + ones = 14, tens - ones = 4: tens 9, ones 5. 95.

questions.stem: Oli is 3 years old. Uma is 2 times as old as Oli. Val is 2 years older than Uma. How old is Val?
questions.solution: Uma is 2 x 3 = 6. Val is 6 + 2 = 8.

questions.stem: Dee, Jo and Raj have 34 marbles in all. Jo has 2 more marbles than Raj. Dee has 3 more marbles than Jo. How many marbles does Raj have?
questions.solution: Imagine Jo and Dee each give away their extras. Jo gives 2, Dee gives 5. That removes 7 marbles, leaving 27. Now all three have the same number: 27 / 3 = 9. So Raj has 9.

questions.stem: Raj is taller than Val. Ben is shorter than Val. Leo is taller than Raj. Which sentence must be true?
questions.solution: The order from tallest to shortest is Leo, Raj, Val, Ben. So Leo is taller than Ben. The other sentences are false.

solve.work: Leo > Raj > Val > Ben. Leo taller than Ben must be true; the others are false.

questions.stem: A pack of pens costs 5 dollars and a notebook costs 2 dollars. Ava buys 3 packs of pens and 3 notebooks. She pays with 50 dollars. How many dollars of change does she get?
questions.solution: Pens: 3 x 5 = 15. Notebooks: 3 x 2 = 6. Total 21 dollars. Change: 50 - 21 = 29 dollars.

questions.stem: A class has 28 children, and 12 of them are boys. Then 4 girls leave for a music lesson and 4 boys come in from another class. How many more boys than girls are in the room now?
questions.solution: Girls at first: 28 - 12 = 16. Girls now: 16 - 4 = 12. Boys now: 12 + 4 = 16. Difference: 16 - 12 = 4.

questions.stem: Fay has 4 boxes with 15 pencils in each box. Fay gives 6 pencils to each of 4 friends. How many pencils does Fay have left?
questions.solution: Pencils at first: 4 x 15 = 60. Given away: 4 x 6 = 24. Left: 60 - 24 = 36.

questions.stem: On Monday Ana reads 13 pages. Each day after that, Ana reads 3 more pages than the day before. How many pages does Ana read from Monday to Thursday altogether?
questions.solution: The pages each day: 13, 16, 19, 22. Add them: 13 + 16 + 19 + 22 = 70.

questions.stem: A baker bakes 8 trays of rolls with 12 rolls on each tray. 36 rolls are sold. The rest are put into bags of 6 rolls. How many bags are filled?
questions.solution: Rolls baked: 8 x 12 = 96. After selling 36: 96 - 36 = 60. Bags: 60 / 6 = 10.

questions.stem: 3 friends share the cost of a plant and a card equally. The plant costs 16 dollars and the card costs 2 dollars. How many dollars does each friend pay?
questions.solution: Total cost: 16 + 2 = 18 dollars. Shared between 3 friends: 18 / 3 = 6 dollars each.

questions.skill: Working backwards and guess and check
questions.stem: I think of a number. I double it, then subtract 3, then add 10. My answer is 35. What number did I think of?
questions.solution: Work backwards, undoing the last step first. Undo "add 10": 35 - 10 = 25. Undo "subtract 3": 25 + 3 = 28. Undo "double": half of 28 is 14.

questions.skill: Working backwards and guess and check
questions.stem: Kim has 12 coins. Each coin is a dime (10 cents) or a nickel (5 cents). Together the coins are worth 85 cents. How many of the coins are dimes?
questions.solution: Guess and check. If all 12 coins were nickels they would be worth 60 cents. Each dime swapped in for a nickel adds 5 cents. The difference is 85 - 60 = 25, so 5 coins are dimes. Check: 5 dimes = 50, 7 nickels = 35, total 85.

solve.work: All nickels = 60 cents; each dime adds 5: 25/5 = 5 dimes. 50+35=85.

questions.skill: Working backwards and guess and check
questions.stem: Zoe spent half of Zoe's money on a book. Then Zoe spent 7 dollars on lunch. Now Zoe has 5 dollars left. How many dollars did Zoe have at the start?
questions.solution: Work backwards. Before lunch: 5 + 7 = 12 dollars. That was half of the money, so at the start: 12 x 2 = 24 dollars.

solve.work: Before lunch 5+7=12; that is half, so 24.

questions.skill: Working backwards and guess and check
questions.stem: Ben thinks of a number. He adds 5, then subtracts 2, then doubles the result. He gets 26. What number did Ben think of?
questions.solution: Work backwards. Undo "double": 26 / 2 = 13. Undo "subtract 2": 13 + 2 = 15. Undo "add 5": 15 - 5 = 10.

questions.skill: Working backwards and guess and check
questions.stem: A farm has 8 animals. They are chickens (2 legs each) and cows (4 legs each). The animals have 24 legs altogether. How many cows are there?
questions.solution: Guess and check. If all 8 animals were chickens there would be 16 legs. Each cow instead of a chicken adds 2 legs. 24 - 16 = 8, so there are 4 cows. Check: 4 cows have 16 legs and 4 chickens have 8 legs; the total is 24.

solve.work: All chickens = 16 legs; each cow adds 2: 8/2 = 4 cows. 4x4 + 4x2 = 24.

questions.skill: Working backwards and guess and check
questions.stem: 5 equal books and a box that weighs 3 kilograms together weigh 13 kilograms. How many kilograms does one of the books weigh?
questions.solution: Take the box away: 13 - 3 = 10 kilograms for the 5 books. Share equally: 10 / 5 = 2 kilograms each.
